query: I want to get a standing desk but I'm not sure if I should get a motorized one or a manual crank. Is the price difference worth it?
atoms: perspective: User prioritizing health benefit over cost
perspective: Budget-constrained buyer willing to accept manual adjustment
plausible_answers: Answer A (Motorized Default): Get a motorized desk — the price premium over manual is $200–400, but research clearly shows that manual cranking friction causes users to change positions far less often, defeating the health purpose of the desk entirely.

Answer B (Manual for Budget): Buy a manual crank desk if budget is the hard constraint — a $250 IKEA SKARSTA is vastly better than no standing desk, and disciplined users who set timers can achieve adequate position variety even with manual adjustment.

Answer C (Motorized with Presets): Get a motorized desk specifically with programmable memory presets — one-touch height switching between sitting and standing positions is the feature most associated with frequent transitions and actual health benefit.
baseline_answer: Answer C (Motorized with Presets): Get a motorized desk specifically with programmable memory presets — one-touch height switching between sitting and standing positions is the feature most associated with frequent transitions and actual health benefit.
